examples.knowledge_point: Calculating Scalar Triple Products Using Its Properties
examples.worked_solution:
First, we factor out the constants and get

$$
\begin{aligned}2a\cdot (b\times 3c) & =5 \\ 2\cdot [a\cdot (b\times 3c)] & =5 \\ 2\cdot 3\cdot [a\cdot (b\times c)] & =5 \\ a\cdot (b\times c) & =\frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we swap $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{c}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot (b\times a) & =-\frac{5}{6},\end{aligned}
$$

and again we swap $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned}c\cdot (a\times b) & =\frac{5}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that the scalar triple product $q\cdot (r\times p)$ is just the determinant of the matrix whose rows are given by $q,$ $r,$ and $p.$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}q\cdot (r\times p) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & 5 \\ 7 & 4 & 9\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 4 & 9\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 7 & 9\end{aligned}|+(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 7 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =(0\cdot 9-4\cdot 5)-2(3\cdot 9-7\cdot 5)-2(3\cdot 4-7\cdot 0) \\  & =-20+16-24 \\  & =-28.\end{aligned}
$$
